These desync strategies inject or fragment packets below the VPN socket and only work on rooted devices with root mode enabled.
Injects a spoofed TCP reset to desynchronise stateful DPI tracking.
Reorders several segments at once to break reassembly-based inspection.
Splits packets at the IP layer so inspectors never see the full payload.
A single local listener accepts both SOCKS5 and HTTP CONNECT connections; defaults to port 2080.

The proxy will accept connections from other devices on your local network. Keep the access token private — anyone with it can route traffic through this device.

Banking, delivery, and government apps bypass the VPN to avoid detection issues.
Route all traffic through VPN with no app exclusions. Prevents spyware modules from sending traffic directly, but Russian apps may detect the VPN.
When enabled, all traffic goes through the tunnel. Per-app exclusions are disabled in this mode.
Apps in all Android profiles (including Work Profile and Knox) can detect that a VPN is active. For full isolation, use a separate device for Russian apps.
When tethering is active, Android runs a local DNS server that bypasses the VPN. Apps may use this to send tracking beacons outside the tunnel.

Launcher-controlled mask used for this app icon on the current device.
Your launcher decides the final icon mask. RIPDPI can switch icon artwork, but the home app keeps control of the visible shape.
Different launchers can show circle, squircle, rounded-square, or custom icon masks.
If the icon artwork changes, your launcher may need a refresh before the new mask preview appears.
Offline network diagnostics and connection toolkit for Android.
RIPDPI builds on the open-source hufrea/ripdpi project and keeps all routing and configuration local to this device.
What is stored on this device, how long it is kept, and when it leaves the device.
What is stored on this device
Network diagnostics: transport type, signal strength, DNS configuration
DPI detection results: failure classifications, strategy effectiveness
Performance metrics: RTT measurements, retry counts, traffic statistics
Network identity: hashed fingerprint of network characteristics (Wi-Fi SSID, carrier info)
Device context: Android version, device model, app version, permission states
Optional: public IP address (only during manual diagnostic scans)
No browsing history, URL content, packet payloads, credentials, or TLS secrets in normal diagnostics
No user accounts: the app works without sign-in
No data is sent to external servers automatically
No analytics, crash reporting, or advertising SDKs
All data stays on your device in a local database
You can disable passive monitoring in advanced settings
Export archives, log files, and shares are only created when you explicitly request them

Exported summaries, manifests, and reports redact IP addresses, Wi-Fi identifiers, and support context. Raw packet captures are stored and exported separately, never embedded in redacted diagnostics archives.
You control what is saved or shared, who receives it, and when to delete saved exports outside app storage
